# DEVICE CAPABILITIES — Galaxy S25 Ultra (SM-S938B)

**Status: MEASURED on Pol's phone** — generated by the app's own inspector (1.1.0-debug 14:24, re-run with 1.1.1 19:56 and 1.1.2 21:30).
Raw files: `device-reports/2026-11-22_SM-S938B/` · machine-readable copy: `DEVICE_CAPABILITIES.json`.
This is what Camera2 / MediaCodec give a **third-party app**, not Samsung's stock-camera spec sheet.
The report contains no photos, audio, location, accounts or serial numbers.

Device: SM-S938B (`pa3q`), Snapdragon SM8750, **Android 17 (API 37)**, build CP2A.260605.016.S938BXXUDDZJB,
security patch 2026-10-05. Thermal status at the time: 1 (light). Concurrent camera pairs: {0,1}, {0,3}.

## Cameras a third-party app can open
| id | What it is | Level | Eq. focal | f/ | ISO | Shutter | Manual / Kelvin WB / RAW / 10-bit | Zoom |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | back **logical** camera (ultra-wide id 2, main id 5, 3× id 6, 5× id 7) | LEVEL_3 | 22.3 mm | 1.7 fixed | 12–3200 | 1/11 977 s – 0.176 s | yes / yes / yes / HLG10 | 0.6–10× |
| 1 | front | FULL | 25.5 mm | 2.2 fixed | 25–3200 | 1/13 727 s – 0.417 s | yes / yes / yes / HLG10 | 1–8× |
| 2 | back ultra-wide on its own | LIMITED | 13.3 mm | 1.9 fixed | 19–3200 | 1/11 977 s – 0.176 s | yes / yes / yes / HLG10 | 1–8× |
| 3 | front, narrower crop | FULL | 30.1 mm | 2.2 fixed | 25–3200 | 1/20 396 s – 0.339 s | yes / yes / yes / HLG10 | 1–8× |

- Lens presets that are real lenses on camera 0: **0.6×, 1×, 2.74×, 5.06×** (61 mm and 112.7 mm equivalents).
  The camera HAL decides which lens streams. 1.1.1 self-test (evening, indoors): 0.6× → ultra-wide (2) and 1× → main (5)
  as expected, but at 2.74× it stayed on the main sensor and at 5.06× it used the 3× tele (6). Samsung falls back to a
  wider lens in low light or at close focus. 1.1.2 zoom sweep in room light (ISO 1156, 1/50 s, subject 3.5 m):
  **2× → main · 3× → 3× tele · 5.06× → 5× tele** — the HAL switches to the 3× tele only from 3.0×, not at its native
  2.74×, so the lens button uses 3.0× from 1.1.3.
- Physical ids 5/6/7 are only reachable through camera 0's zoom; the ultra-wide is also exposed as id 2.
- Apertures are fixed on every lens. AE and AF accept 1 metering region; AWB regions are not supported.
- **OIS control is not exposed** (mode list = OFF only), so the app hides its OIS toggle; video stabilisation
  ON and PREVIEW_STABILIZATION are offered on the back cameras.
- ZSL request key present on all cameras. Extensions offered: FACE_RETOUCH, BOKEH, NIGHT (not used by the app).
- Active array 4080×3060 (12 MP binned); **ULTRA_HIGH_RESOLUTION_SENSOR is not advertised → no 200 MP for third-party apps.**

## Video
- Modes this app can record (camera + encoder agree): **4K 24/30, 1080p 24/30/60, 720p 24/30/60, H.264 and HEVC**
  (camera 3: 1080p/720p only).
- **No 4K60 and no 8K through standard Camera2.** The encoders can do 3840×2160@60 and 7680×4320@30, but the camera
  HAL's minimum frame duration for normal recording rules out 4K60, and 7680×4320 is not offered as a recording
  size. Confirmed by the 1.1.1 inspector (`video_max_fps_by_size`): **3840×2160 → 30 fps, 1920×1080 → 60, 1280×720 → 60**;
  `ultra_high_resolution_sensor: false`.
- High-speed (slow-motion) sessions exist: **1080p and 720p at 120 and 240 fps** on cameras 0 and 2, 120 fps on
  the front cameras. Not used by v1.1 yet.
- 10-bit: HLG10 dynamic-range profile on all cameras; hardware HEVC HDR encoder `c2.qti.hevc.encoder.hdr` (≤4096 px).
  Not used by v1.1 yet.

## Encoders (hardware)
| Encoder | Max size | Max bitrate | 1080×1920@30 | 1440×2560@30 | 4K60 | 8K30 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| c2.qti.avc.encoder (H.264) | 8192×8192 | 220 Mbps | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| c2.qti.hevc.encoder | 8192×8192 | 160 Mbps | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| c2.qti.hevc.encoder.hdr | 4096×4096 | 160 Mbps | yes | yes | yes | no |

AAC encoding is software (c2.android / c2.sec). AV1 and APV encoders are software only.

## Speech
The phone has an on-device recognizer; Thai is supported but **not installed** (only en-US). Voice Shutter does not
use it (its own offline matcher), so this does not affect the app.

## Verified by the 1.1.1 self-test (19:57)
4K30 HEVC and 1080p60 H.264 recording with sound, StoryMax export from the 4K HEVC clip with AAC copied as-is,
microphone loop at 16 kHz. Steady-state shutter lag ~0.31 s with `CONTROL_ENABLE_ZSL` on *and* off — the HAL ignores
the ZSL key for this app; 1.1.2 measures `TEMPLATE_ZERO_SHUTTER_LAG` as the alternative. The first microphone buffers
are exact zeros (the 1.1.1 report showed a −180 dB floor); 1.1.2 ignores them.

## Verified by the 1.1.2 self-test (21:30)
`TEMPLATE_ZERO_SHUTTER_LAG` is ignored too (137 ms vs. 142 ms with the ZSL key and 149 ms without); start-up zeros
from the microphone are now ignored (background −63.9 dBFS).
